whatWasMissing.note: The model has been able to switch cylinders since the migration began — InputIntent carries switchGasIndex and applyGasSwitchIntent implements the rules, with unit coverage in tests/unit/dive-model.test.ts. Nothing in the client ever set the field, so a two-cylinder dive could be configured on the setup screen and then stayed on the first cylinder for the whole dive.
whatWasMissing.consequence: #158 shipped multi-cylinder configuration whose only effect in the dive was the starting gas.

boundsPortedFromTheOracle.keyBindings: src/game-loop.js TASK-019 — `for (var i = 0; i < tankCount; i++)` over String(i + 1), so 1 to 6 and no further; MAX_TANKS is 6
boundsPortedFromTheOracle.refusalRules: src/game-loop.js `i !== activeTank && tanks[i].gasRemaining > 0`, which src/core/dive-model.ts applyGasSwitchIntent already implements, plus its own refusal of any switch while ccr is set
boundsPortedFromTheOracle.rowVisibility: src/ui.js and src/touch.js show cylinder slots only where the mode has more than one cylinder

deliberateDesign.rulesStayInTheModel: The controller decides nothing about whether a switch is allowed. It passes an index; src/core/dive-model.ts refuses the active cylinder, an empty one and CCR. Duplicating those checks in the UI would have created a second place for them to drift.
deliberateDesign.emptyCylinderStaysVisible: Disabled rather than removed, and it keeps its contrast instead of fading to the usual grey. An empty cylinder is not a broken control, and a cylinder that vanishes mid-dive is worse than one that says why it cannot be chosen.
deliberateDesign.delegatedClickHandler: The buttons do not exist when the dive starts — the first frame builds them from the state — so the click listener sits on the container. A listener per button would have to be rebound on every rebuild.
deliberateDesign.buttonsBuiltOnce: syncTankControls creates the buttons only when the count changes and thereafter updates attributes. Rebuilding them each frame would discard focus sixty times a second, and unlike the setup screen there is no re-render to restore it from.
deliberateDesign.appliedAtOnce: The switch is applied when pressed, not sampled at the next step. See reviewRound1.queueWasALatestValueSlot for why the alternatives were rejected.

sliceBoundary.deviation: Gas info is its own PR. It is five rendered pages with their own cycling rules — src/state.js infoPageMode 0-5, skipping the tanks page below four cylinders, toggling 0<->5 in CCR, and unavailable in rec entirely — which is larger than the switch and unrelated to it. The slicing in an issue is a hint, not a contract.
sliceBoundary.stillOutstandingInThisIssue: gas info (I), fast-forward (F), torch as a first-class intent, CCR setpoint ([ ]) and bailout (B), and the HUD additions the issue lists: active cylinder, loop PO2 vs setpoint, scrubber time, bailout state, fast-forward indicator.

notTestedAndWhy.gasSwitchNotification: Legacy shows a two-second 'GAS SWITCH -> T{n}' toast and resets bestGasAlerted and fastForwardActive. The toast belongs with the HUD additions and fastForwardActive with the fast-forward slice; neither exists yet, so neither is reproduced.
notTestedAndWhy.noUnitTests: What this slice adds is the immediate switch path and the DOM sync, and both need a running animation frame. The node test environment has no requestAnimationFrame — tests/unit already notes this for destroy() — so the coverage is e2e, where the real loop runs, rather than a mock that would assert the mock. The model half, DiveModel.switchGas, is reachable without a frame and its rules are already covered by tests/unit/dive-model.test.ts through applyGasSwitchIntent.

counterCheck.method: One revert at a time, restoring the actual previous design rather than breaking the code conveniently, with the build result read before each run.

cases.immediateSwitch: the single-slot design restored in full — the swallowed-switch test fails
cases.rowWrapping: the width cap removed — the overlap tests fail
cases.dockStacking: the hint anchored absolutely again — the desktop overlap test fails

counterCheck.oneTestProvedNothingAtFirst: The swallowed-switch test used the review's own example, 2 then an out-of-range 6. The new tankCount gate stops 6 in the controller, so the slot was never overwritten and the test passed with the old design restored — the P3 fix had masked the P2 scenario. Rewritten on three cylinders with 2 then 3, asserting both switches are recorded in order, which is the general case the review also named.
counterCheck.aContrivedRevertWasDiscarded: The first attempt at the immediate-switch revert simply made index 1 a no-op. That would have shown the test can fail, not that it tests the fix, so it was replaced by a faithful restoration of the slot design across all four of its edits.

durableProvenance.why: measuredCommit is a branch commit, and every PR here is squash-merged with the branch deleted, so it becomes unreachable from main the moment this lands. Checked across the repository: all six evidence artifacts record a measuredCommit that origin/main cannot reach, so the usual `git rev-parse <measuredCommit>^{tree}` recipe is reproducible only for whoever still has the branch. Raised as a P3 on PR #176 for one artifact; it turned out to be structural.
durableProvenance.check: Subtree hashes survive the squash, because the squash commit carries the same content. After this merges, run `git rev-parse <squash-merge-commit>:src <squash-merge-commit>:tests <squash-merge-commit>:scripts` and compare with the three below. Verified on two already-merged PRs: #179 (115c33f vs 3340d60) and #176 (12b567e vs 00c709c), all three subtrees identical in both.
durableProvenance.caveat: This holds because the only commit after the measured one adds this artifact, which touches nothing under src, tests or scripts. If a later commit on the branch changes any of them, these hashes stop matching and the measurement no longer describes what shipped — which is the point of recording them.

queueWasALatestValueSlot.finding: #requestedTankIndex held one index until the next whole-second step, so a second press inside that second overwrote the first and the intermediate switch never happened. The PR text claimed a press between steps 'is not lost', which held only for a single press.
queueWasALatestValueSlot.fix: DiveModel.switchGas() applies the switch when pressed, as legacy does in the frame it reads the key (game-loop.js TASK-019). Nothing is held, so nothing can be overwritten.
queueWasALatestValueSlot.queueRejected: A FIFO queue was the other option. It keeps both presses but emits two gas-switch events a second apart for something the diver did at once, and it leaves the up-to-one-second latency this PR had to explain away. Applying at once removes both.
queueWasALatestValueSlot.unchanged: applyGasSwitchIntent still decides whether a switch is allowed; switchGas adds only the guard that a failed dive does not switch, which advanceDiveStep applies too.

rowRanUnderTheDpad.finding: Measured at 390px: five overlapping pairs, cylinders 4-6 beneath the left, descend and right buttons, both at z-index 4 with the D-pad painting over them. The keyboard hint shared the same bottom-left offsets, so at desktop width it was drawn across the row.
rowRanUnderTheDpad.whyCiStayedGreen: The touch-target test compared the cylinder buttons with each other and with nothing else. Same shape of mistake as measuring only rec for touch targets in #158: the check looked exactly where the author was already looking.
rowRanUnderTheDpad.fix: The row wraps within a width cap that keeps it clear of the controls, and the hint and the row are stacked in one dock instead of both being anchored absolutely — a column cannot overlap itself, which beats tuning two sets of offsets against each other. A new test asserts no cylinder button overlaps any other control, at 390px and at desktop width.
rowRanUnderTheDpad.staleCommentRemoved: A CSS comment claimed the row sat 'opposite the D-pad, so a thumb is not on top of the ascent keys'. That was the sentence the measurement disproved.

p3s.helperComment: The two-cylinder helper's doc comment described a 50% mix it never configured; both cylinders are air and only the pressure differs.
p3s.keyBinding: The controller bound 1-6 regardless of how many cylinders existed. Legacy iterates to tankCount, so a digit past the cylinder count is now not a dive key at all and the client leaves it alone rather than claiming and discarding it.

reviewRound1.switchDepth: The reviewer agreed this does not block the slice and belongs with the deferred gas-info path. Unchanged, still noted on #163.

controlsOfferedAfterFailure.finding: switchGas refuses a switch while failure.reason is set, but syncTankControls hid the row only for CCR or a single cylinder, so a failed multi-cylinder dive kept enabled buttons, and the digit keys were still claimed with preventDefault(). An action offered that could not happen.
controlsOfferedAfterFailure.oracle: Legacy shows its touch UI only while gameState === 'diving' and takes it away at gameover. #163's scope says controls appear only when the dive state allows them.
controlsOfferedAfterFailure.fix: The row hides on presentation.status === 'failed'. The digit keys are not claimed there either: claiming a key means calling preventDefault() on it, so it has to be a key that does something. The same predicate covers digits past the cylinder count.
controlsOfferedAfterFailure.testOracleHadToChange: Asserting the model is unchanged proves nothing about the keys — switchGas refuses either way, so that assertion passes whether or not the key was claimed, and the counter-check said so before the test was believed. The test now reads defaultPrevented from a listener registered after the controller's, which is the only thing that distinguishes the two.
controlsOfferedAfterFailure.counterCheck: Both halves fail with their own fix reverted: the row stops hiding, and the key is claimed again. Build result read first.

reviewRound2.staleDocumentation: The PR body and one evidence field still described the queued design that round 1 replaced. Both corrected; notTestedAndWhy.noUnitTests no longer speaks of a queue.
